newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Allstate growth slower than planned.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Allstate growth slower than planned.

text.p: Allstate Corp chairman Jerry Choate said second quarter revenues from core operations grew more slowly than he had hoped, although he was pleased with the insurance company's gain in operating earnings.
"If you look at our performance, the only thing that concerns me at all is the top line," Choate said Tuesday in a telephone interview. "I would like to see it moving faster."
He added that Allstate's long-term target is to grow revenues by about eight to 10 percent a year.

Excluding capital gains and businesses that were sold, Allstate's premiums written on personal and liability coverage rose about four percent in the second quarter. Premiums earned gained about five percent.

Overall, Allstate's property-liability revenues were $5.17 billion, down 5.5 percent from a year ago. But the decline reflects lower realized capital gains and the sale of commercial and reinsurance businesses in 1996.
"The top line was a little bit below expectations," A.G. Edwards analyst Jeffrey Hopson said.
Hopson said Allstate's smaller life and annuity business was growing at about 10 to 12 percent on an annual basis.

Consolidated second quarter revenues for Allstate fell four percent to $6.07 billion, reflecting the sales of commercial and reinsurance businesses in 1996, lower realized capital gains and the impact of catastrophe management initiatives.
Allstate has been reducing its exposure to catastrophe losses in the wake of claims from Hurricane Andrew in 1992 and a California earthquake in 1994.
Allstate's operating earnings in the second quarter gained 19 percent to $575 million.
"Operating income was quite good," Choate said. "I think everybody would recognize that."
Net income in the quarter dropped 15.8 percent to $643 million from $764 million, reflecting in part a reduction in after-tax realized capital gains to $70 million from $273 million.
Property and liability, Allstate's largest division, posted a 20.7 percent rise in operating income to $489 million. Life and annuity operating income gained 9.3 percent to $94 million.

To drive the top line growth in the future, Choate said Allstate has undertaken several initiatives including detailed consumer marketing studies and becoming more aggressive in California where it recently reduced prices to "kick start" its business.
To grow its life and annuity operations further, Choate said Allstate is looking to sell traditional life coverage to more of its property and liability customers.
